messages.author: 8dafe35eb614235f
messages.subject: left_join by numeric column
parts:
Is there a way to make dplyr::left_join() join two tables on numeric columns, like LibreOffice Calc's vlookup(..., sort order = 1) does? While left_join() mirrors what vlookup(..., sort order = 0) does, I can't figure out an easy way to have it join on a row with the next lowest numeric value. Here's a toy example:

grade.book <- data.frame(
  PERSON = c("Bobby", "Jane", "Johnny", "Luisa"), 
  PERC = c(67.8, 78.9, 89.1, 90.2)
)

grade.scale <- data.frame(
  SCORE = c(90, 80, 70, 60, 0), 
  GRADE = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "F")
)

left_join(grade.book, grade.scale, by = c("PERC" = "SCORE"))

  PERSON PERC GRADE
1  Bobby 67.8  <NA>
2   Jane 78.9  <NA>
3 Johnny 89.1  <NA>
4  Luisa 90.2  <NA>

But, I'd like it to give me:

  PERSON PERC GRADE
1  Bobby 67.8     D
2   Jane 78.9     C
3 Johnny 89.1     B
4  Luisa 90.2     A

One work-around involves two "for" loops and an "if" statement:

all.grades <- c()
for (i in 1:nrow(grade.book)) {
  cur.perc <- grade.book[i, 'PERC']
  for (j in 1:nrow(grade.scale)) {
    cur.score <- grade.scale[j, 'SCORE']
    if (cur.perc > cur.score) {
      all.grades[i] <- as.character(grade.scale$GRADE[j])
      break
    } 
  } # next possible grade
} # next person in gradebook
grade.book$GRADE <- all.grades

Is there an argument in left_join() that I'm missing that might do this?

Thanks in advance for any help, even on making the work-around shorter.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: left_join by numeric column
parts:
Hi Earl,

You want a non-equi join, which dplyr doesn't currently support. We're
thinking about it for dplyr 0.5.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: left_join by numeric column
parts:
Thank you Hadley and Brandon. I was able to get it to work with data.table:

library("data.table")
library("dplyr")

grade.book <- data.table(

setkey(grade.scale, SCORE)

grade.scale[grade.book, roll = Inf] %>%
  select(PERSON, PERC = SCORE, GRADE) %>%
  arrange(PERSON)

I look forward to being able to do this with dplyr, if it is added in 0.5, as magrittr's pipe operator is great. 

Thanks Hadley (and Romain) for the great dplyr package. It has made data manipulation almost effortless.

messages.author: e3fc8587db796618
messages.subject: Re: left_join by numeric column
parts:
I think it can be done by reordering the grade.scale and using cut:
> grade.scale <- data.frame(
+     SCORE = rev(c(90, 80, 70, 60, 0)), 
+     GRADE = rev(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "F"))
+ )
> grade.book %>% mutate(GRADE=cut(PERC,c(grade.scale$SCORE,100),labels=grade.scale$GRADE))

PERSON PERC GRADE
1  Bobby 67.8     D
2   Jane 78.9     C
3 Johnny 89.1     B
4  Luisa 90.2     A

More generally, as long as the "labels" are unique to the rows in the grade.scale,
I think you can implement the non equi-join by inner joining the above result back with grade.scale (e.g).

> grade.scale <- data.frame(
+     SCORE = rev(c(90, 80, 70, 60, 0)), 
+     GRADE = rev(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "F")),
+     RETAKECLASS=rev(c("N","N","MAYBE","Y","Y"))
+ )
> grade.book %>% mutate(GRADE=cut(PERC,c(grade.scale$SCORE,100),labels=grade.scale$GRADE)) %>% inner_join(grade.scale)
Joining by: "GRADE"
  PERSON PERC GRADE SCORE RETAKECLASS
1  Bobby 67.8     D    60           Y
2   Jane 78.9     C    70       MAYBE
3 Johnny 89.1     B    80           N
4  Luisa 90.2     A    90           N
Warning message:
joining factors with different levels, coercing to character vector
